subject: Banking
title: The Gold Standard
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Gold Standard usable.

hook.text: For 200 years, a country's money was a promise: bring this note to the bank and we will give you gold.

buildup.text: Britain adopted the gold standard in 1821. Other nations followed. Exchange rates became fixed by gold ratios.

discovery.text: The gold standard prevented inflation because governments couldn't print more money than their gold reserves allowed.

twist.text: It also prevented growth. During recessions, a gold-limited money supply made economic downturns longer and deeper.

climax.text: The gold standard traded flexibility for stability. When crises demanded flexible response, gold was a cage.

punchline.text: Gold backed every dollar. Stable, until the economy needed room to breathe.

quiz.question: What was the main limitation of the gold standard?
options: It prevented flexible monetary response during recessions

details.summary: The gold standard linked currency values to specific amounts of physical gold, providing price stability for decades but also constraining governments' ability to respond to economic crises. Most countries abandoned it during the 20th century.
details.whyItMatters: The gold standard debate continues to shape monetary policy discussions. Understanding its benefits and failures explains why modern central banks use fiat currency and why some still argue for returning to gold.
takeaways: Britain formally adopted the gold standard in 1821, and it spread globally
The system constrained money supply to gold reserves, limiting inflation
Gold standard rigidity deepened the Great Depression as countries could not print money

faq.question: Why did countries abandon the gold standard?
faq.answer: The gold standard prevented governments from expanding the money supply during crises. During the Great Depression, countries that left gold first recovered fastest because they could print money and lower interest rates to stimulate their economies.

faq.question: Could the gold standard be restored today?
faq.answer: Most economists say no. There is not enough gold to back the current global money supply, and the rigidity would prevent central banks from responding to crises. However, gold standard advocates argue it would prevent the inflation that fiat currency enables.
